method.over_index: Exact replica of an/vis_cbsa.py with only the sheet name changed for 2025 (TABLE 56): rows from index 3 whose first cell is non-empty and second cell numeric; columns TOTAL (1), O‘AHU (2), MAUI island (4), KAUA‘I (7), HAWAI‘I ISLAND (8) (header text asserted); Salt Lake City UT + Provo-Orem UT + Ogden-Clearfield UT summed into "Salt Lake City–Provo–Ogden UT" (67 rows -> 65 metros); base(island) = sum island / sum TOTAL over the 65 metros; share = metro island / metro TOTAL; idx = share / base.
method.lists: "top15_2025_with_change" = 15 largest metros by 2025 island visitors with 2024 value, ranks, change, % change and DBEDT Table 57 % (Utah combined has no Table 57 row). "over_index_<year>_at_threshold" = all metros with island visitors >= 20,000 (Oʻahu, Maui), 10,000 (Kauaʻi), 15,000 (Hawaiʻi Island), sorted by idx (the report thresholds). "vis_cbsa_replica_2025_*" = vis_cbsa.py's own output (n >= 10,000 on every island, top 10). "pooled_2024_2025_over_index" = supplementary: both years' counts summed before computing idx; threshold applied to the two-year average.
method.states: TABLE 53 (2025) and 2024 TABLE 52, 49 states + D.C.; supplementary state idx uses the same formula with base over all 50 rows.
method.japan_canada: Region/province visitor counts and ISLANDS VISITED rows; idx = (group island visitors / group visitors) / (sum island / sum visitors over groups). Japan base is the 9-region sum (international flights only).
checks: computed metro % changes vs DBEDT TABLE 57: max diff 0.0 pct-pts over the 64 non-Utah metros x 5 columns (TOTAL and 4 islands)
computed state % changes vs TABLE 54: max diff 0.0e+00 pct-pts
2024 state totals in 2025 TABLE 19 equal 2024 TABLE 52 (max diff 0.0); 2025 TABLE 19 equals TABLE 53 (max diff 0.0)
sum of 50 state rows 2025 = 7,415,500 = TABLE 19 United States
Table 21 2025 and 2024 metro totals equal TABLE 56 / 2024 TABLE 55 totals for every common metro

notes: The 2024 workbook on DBEDT's official site is byte-identical (sha256 86bf9ca5711671f3a4333bba15a0da06d70df361269c68d8951cf94acad0a35c) to the mirror copy used for an/vis_cbsa.py, so every 2024 visitor-metro figure in the report stands as published.

Table numbering changed in 2025: the CBSA-by-island table is TABLE 56 (TABLE 55 is now a new "Length of Stay by Island and State" table). an/vis_cbsa.py hard-codes "TABLE 55"; run unchanged on the 2025 workbook it would read the wrong sheet and fail its Utah assert. Japan (23) and Canada (25) kept their numbers; state-by-island moved from 52 to 53.
The 2025 workbook did not revise 2024: our 2025-vs-2024 % changes computed from the 2024 workbook equal DBEDT's own TABLE 57 and TABLE 54 to floating-point precision.

Same 67 CBSAs in both years, identical names. TABLE 56 uses older OMB titles (e.g. "San Francisco-Oakland-Hayward CA"); TABLE 21 uses 2023 titles (e.g. "San Francisco-Oakland-Fremont CA", "Salt Lake City-Murray UT", "Provo-Orem-Lehi UT", "Ogden UT") and adds Omaha NE-IA, which is not in TABLE 56. TABLE 21 RANK follows 2024 arrivals order (verified).

Island columns count visitors who visited each island; multi-island visitors appear in several columns, so island columns do not sum to TOTAL. Values are survey-weighted estimates (fractional in the workbook); outputs are rounded to whole visitors. MAUI is the island, not Maui County.

The base is the pooled share across the 65 listed metros only (79% of U.S. domestic-flight visitors in 2025), not all U.S. visitors. idx 1.30 = 30% more of that metro's visitors go to the island than the listed-metro average.

Metro-level year-over-year swings in DBEDT's own figures are large (TOTAL: Albuquerque -39.2%, Dallas-Fort Worth -38.5%, Phoenix -33.5%, Boulder +39.1%, Denver +36.1%; island cells larger still, e.g. Phoenix to Maui -45.8%, Denver to Kauaʻi +69.2%). Single-year over-index ranks move accordingly (Minneapolis on Maui 1.31 -> 1.09). DBEDT publishes no margins of error for these cells; the pooled 2024+2025 index is the steadier signal.

Changes vs 2024 that matter for the report: Oʻahu over-index leader is now Baltimore (1.35) ahead of Atlanta (1.26), San Antonio (1.25) and Washington DC (1.24; was 1.33); Maui leaders are Portland (1.22) and Denver (1.20), Chicago stays in (1.16; was 1.25), Minneapolis (1.31 -> 1.09) and Dallas-Fort Worth (1.14 -> 1.11) fall back; Kauaʻi leaders Denver (1.67) and Salt Lake City–Provo–Ogden (1.47) strengthen; Hawaiʻi Island keeps Anchorage on top (1.41; 2024 1.42) with Boston (1.31) entering at 17,188 visitors (was 14,097, below the 15K threshold). By count, New York rises to #4 for Oʻahu (San Diego falls from #4 to #6) and San Francisco–Oakland passes Los Angeles for #1 on Hawaiʻi Island; Seattle is still #3 for every island (460,243 total visitors in 2025, up from 444,354).

The Oʻahu list (min 20,000) is still led by military and federal centers (Baltimore, San Antonio, Washington DC), now joined by Atlanta (1.26) and Riverside–San Bernardino (1.21); Virginia Beach has the highest Oʻahu index (1.39) but only 13,030 visitors. Official travel may explain part of these leads. Visitors are a signal, not a count of buyers.

Japan TABLE 23 covers Japanese visitors on international flights only (743,614 of 749,596 Japan MMA visitors) and has no total column; 97.8% of them visit Oʻahu. Canada TABLE 25 covers all Canada MMA visitors (389,241, including 73,912 who arrived on domestic flights via the U.S. mainland); province columns sum to the total.

Small cells: every output value below 20 visitors is listed in results.small_cells and in each state/region row's flag_lt20. All but two are Molokaʻi/Lānaʻi cells (DBEDT itself notes Molokaʻi/Lānaʻi samples are small); the other two are Okinawa-to-Kauaʻi = 0 in both years. No metro cell for the four main islands is below 2,000 in either year (smallest: Modesto to Kauaʻi 2025, 2,138).
gaps: No host blocked any request; no bot checks, logins or tokens encountered.
DBEDT publishes no sample sizes or standard errors for metro-by-island cells, so year-over-year changes cannot be tested for significance.
Japan regions only (9 regions); no prefecture/city detail. Korea, China and other foreign markets have no sub-national tables.
TABLE 56 lists only 67 CBSAs (79.3% of U.S. domestic-flight visitors in 2025); the remaining 20.7% cannot be split by metro.
The 2025 PDF was downloaded but not parsed for numbers; the workbook is the source. PDF table list confirms "Table 56. 2025 Domestic U.S. Air Visitor Arrivals by Island and Top CBSA".
